rationale: REVISION 2 (council round 2 on 61105914 returned REVISE; only debug_historian objected, both points procedural and both accepted). Added: (i) an explicit pod-verification step — the Go change is inert until an image is rebuilt and rolled, and must be confirmed by grepping the RUNNING pod's binary, never git or the image tag, since a same-tag rebuild ships the node's stale cached binary; (ii) verify and rollback files alongside the migration. Round 1's objections (UUID parse-and-drop-to-NULL; scope creep onto run_discovery_checks_action; missing doc_notes) were all accepted and fixed in revision 1 — editquality and tooling_provenance both approved this round. We cannot currently tell whether any of the platform's judgement agents are any good, because nothing links a judgement to what happened to it. The auditors (content-quality-auditor 7,119 LLM calls, visual-design-auditor 4,032, site-review-agent 3,987) raise site_work_items via write_audit_findings_action, and those items reach real terminal outcomes (live 2026-07-19: 4,570 complete, 278 needs_human_review, 236 unresolved, 152 failed, 50 wont_fix). But the created row records no pointer back to the run that raised it, so the join 'this finding -> this outcome' does not exist. Practical consequence today: an auditor that flags twenty non-issues and one real defect is indistinguishable, in the data, from one that flags twenty real defects — we have no per-agent precision signal, so nobody can tell which auditor is worth its spend or which item_types it over-fires on. This change adds that pointer. Secondary motivation, stated plainly so reviewers can weigh it: the reasoning-dataset workstream needs (reasoning -> outcome) pairs as training/eval labels, and this single field is what makes ~15,000 existing judgement calls per month joinable to ground truth. We are NOT proposing to propagate work_item_id into llm_call_log for these agents — that was our first idea and it was wrong: these agents are item PRODUCERS, not handlers, so no work_item_id exists at their spawn time (verified: none appears as a handler_agent anywhere, and only build-dispatch-loop injects that field). The correct direction is the reverse one, from the created item back to its origin run.

plan.summary: site_work_items records no link back to the orchestration run whose reasoning created it, so agent judgements can never be scored against item outcomes. Add a nullable origin_correlation_id TEXT column (plus a partial index) and populate it at the ONE INSERT path that creates items from LLM findings (write_audit_findings_action), plus a doc_notes entry recording the decision. Nullable, additive, TEXT so no parse can fail: existing rows and all readers are unaffected. Revision 1 narrows scope from 4 edits to 3 and drops the UUID parse.

edits.rationale: A first-class join key belongs in a column, not smuggled into the spec JSONB, which holds the defect's domain data and is read by handlers and verifiers. site_work_items already carries provenance-shaped columns (source, created_by, batch_id) so this follows the established shape. TEXT rather than UUID (revision 1, per editquality): the correlation is stored verbatim so no parse can fail and no legitimate origin can be silently nulled. This matches diagnosis_artifacts.correlation_id, which is deliberately TEXT for the same reason. Nullable with no backfill: historical rows genuinely have no known origin and must read as unknown rather than be guessed at.

This is the path by which every auditor finding becomes a work item, and the one the rationale establishes. params.ExecutionContext carries the correlation id, so no new plumbing is needed. Adding one column to an existing INSERT keeps the change inside the statement that already writes batch_id and created_by. With a TEXT column the value is passed straight through — no parse, no failure mode, and an empty ExecutionContext yields SQL NULL via the same nil check.

Per tooling_provenance: this action is exactly the kind of subject that carries travelling PLAN/NOTES keyed by subject_type+subject_key, and the next person to touch this INSERT needs the decisions recorded, not rediscovered. Written as part of the change, not afterwards.
edits.sketch:
Leave a doc_notes entry (subject_type='action', subject_key='write_audit_findings_action') recording:
 - origin_correlation_id is TEXT and stored VERBATIM; do not add a UUID parse (revision 1 of council 61105914 — a parse can only turn a real origin into an indistinguishable NULL)
 - nullable, no backfill: historical rows have no recoverable origin
 - deliberately NOT part of item_key / idx_swi_dedup — provenance must never affect dedup identity, or the same defect raised by two runs would stop deduplicating
 - the discovery-check creation path (run_discovery_checks_action) deliberately does NOT carry this column: those items come from deterministic predicates, not LLM judgements, so there is no reasoning to join to

edits.rationale: Per debug_historian. The migration is additive and idempotent so the full data-surgery discipline is largely moot, but a production migration should still ship its verify and its undo. Both are trivial here precisely because nothing is mutated — which is the argument for including them, not for skipping them.

Council 61105914 (2026-07-19), reviewer editquality, objection accepted verbatim: 'Choosing UUID for origin_correlation_id, combined with a parse-and-drop-to-NULL strategy in Go, risks silently nulling out legitimate correlation ids that aren't canonical UUID strings, which would quietly undermine the very outcome-join the plan exists to create while looking like normal unknown origin NULLs.'

Council 61105914, reviewer editquality: 'run_discovery_checks_action.go / discovery_checks/registry.go is not established in the rationale as serving those same agents ... edits 3-4 are scope creep onto a path the diagnosis never diagnosed.' Accepted — those edits are removed.

Council 61105914 round 2 (2026-07-19), reviewer debug_historian: 'this must be confirmed by grepping the RUNNING pod's binary for the new symbol ... never by git history or the image tag, since same-tag rebuilds can ship stale binaries.' Accepted — added as an explicit verification step.
plan.risks: site_work_items is a hot table; ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN of a nullable TEXT column with no default is metadata-only on modern Postgres and should not rewrite the table, but a reviewer should confirm the server version and that no long transaction holds a conflicting lock at apply time. The new partial index adds a small write cost on insert. Deliberately NOT touched: idx_swi_dedup and workItemTerminalStatuses in work_items_common.go — this change adds no status and alters no dedup key, so the index/Go-list lockstep contract (which has caused fleet-wide 42P10 before) is untouched. A reviewer should confirm the dedup index does not need the new column: it must not, or the same defect raised by two runs would stop deduplicating. Migration numbering must follow the ledger discipline in bugs_open/007. Backfill is deliberately out of scope: historical rows have no recoverable origin and inventing one would poison the join this creates. Revision 1 residual risk: items created by run_discovery_checks_action will carry NULL origin for ever. That is now intentional and documented, not an oversight — those items come from deterministic checks with no LLM reasoning behind them. If a future change wants provenance there too, it is a separate submission with its own rationale. VERIFICATION (per debug_historian, round 2): the Go edit is inert until a chassis image is rebuilt and rolled. Confirm against the RUNNING pod, never git and never the image tag — `kubectl exec -n ai-persona-system <pod> -- sh -c 'strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -c origin_correlation_id'` must return non-zero — then confirm end-to-end by running one audit and checking the new rows carry a non-NULL origin: `SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE origin_correlation_id IS NOT NULL) FROM site_work_items WHERE created_at > now() - interval '1 hour'`. Order matters: apply the migration BEFORE the image rolls (an INSERT naming a column that does not exist fails at runtime), and expect the column to stay all-NULL in between — that is the correct intermediate state, not a failure.
